title: One Model Family, Two Gold-Level Results: Fine-Tuning Nemotron for IOI and IMO
gist: NVIDIA says fine-tuned Nemotron 3 models reached gold-level at both IOI 2026 (535.4/600) and IMO 2026 (30/42) by combining SFT, RL and generate-verify-refine inference loops, and released checkpoints, datasets and pipelines on Hugging Face.

insights.claim: Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC with SFT and GenCorrect scored 535.4/600 on IOI 2026, above the 361.12 gold threshold and the top human score of 498.27, in a live prospective run that was unofficial and unsupervised and not included in the official ranking.
insights.speaker: Aleksander
insights.so_what: Open-weight model exceeding top human competitive programming score; caveat is that the run was unofficial.

insights.claim: A Nemotron 3 Ultra generate-verify-refine system scored 30/42 at IMO 2026, above the official gold threshold of 29, with proofs graded by official IMO graders and full credit on four of six problems.
insights.speaker: Aleksander
insights.so_what: Officially graded gold-level math proofs from an open model with no formal prover or tools.
insights.locator: Teaching Nemotron to prove, check, and revise

insights.claim: The IMO system worked entirely in natural language, with no formal prover, external tools or internet access.
insights.speaker: Aleksander
insights.so_what: Shows pure language-model reasoning at olympiad-proof level.
insights.locator: Teaching Nemotron to prove, check, and revise

insights.claim: NVIDIA's reusable recipe has four parts: start from a strong Nemotron base, curate domain problems and high-quality reasoning traces, apply standard post-training such as SFT and RL, and pair the specialist with an inference loop that generates, evaluates and improves candidates.
insights.speaker: Aleksander
insights.so_what: Positions open base models plus post-training as a way to build frontier specialists without new foundation models.
insights.quote: We did not need to build a new foundation model for every challenge.

insights.claim: For competitive programming NVIDIA curated 22,000 problems with synthetic reasoning traces to train Nemotron-3-Nano-CC (30B total, 3B active parameters, SFT plus RL) and Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC (550B total, 55B active, SFT only).
insights.speaker: Aleksander
insights.so_what: Gives scale of data and model sizes behind the result; MoE active-parameter ratios around 10%.
insights.locator: From general coding ability to IOI gold

insights.claim: On IOI 2025, Nano rose from 130 points before post-training to 280 after SFT and 291 after RL, reached 468 with GenCorrect (above the 438.3 gold threshold), and Ultra-CC reached 502 with the same test-time strategy.
insights.speaker: Aleksander
insights.so_what: A small model with specialization plus test-time search crosses gold, showing how much capability sits in post-training and inference.

insights.claim: SFT produced most of Nano's gain with RL adding a smaller consistent improvement, and for the stronger Ultra model one SFT epoch outperformed the fully post-trained Nano across IOI, ICPC and LiveCodeBench Pro.
insights.speaker: Aleksander
insights.so_what: Bigger bases need less post-training to beat smaller specialists, favoring scale plus light SFT.

insights.claim: The IMO SFT corpus had 414,890 quality-filtered examples across 15,818 unique proof problems covering generation, refinement, verification and meta-verification, while the RL model trained on 9,597 problems near the model's capability frontier.
insights.speaker: Aleksander
insights.so_what: Training the verifier and critic roles, not just solutions, is central to the approach.

insights.claim: Using complementary SFT and RL checkpoints at IMO was more valuable than simply drawing more samples from one checkpoint; the SFT checkpoint was strongest in the first search round and the RL checkpoint had the best single-checkpoint result.
insights.speaker: Aleksander
insights.so_what: Diversity of specialist checkpoints beats brute-force sampling, a hint for inference compute allocation.
insights.locator: Fine-tuning and test-time compute work together

insights.claim: The medals came from co-designing model, data and inference loop, not from fine-tuning alone or brute-force sampling alone.
insights.speaker: Aleksander
insights.so_what: Value accrues to full-stack system design (train plus inference), supporting NVIDIA's software moat narrative.
insights.quote: They came from co-designing the model, the data, and the inference loop.
insights.locator: Fine-tuning and test-time compute work together

insights.claim: NVIDIA released the Nemotron Labs IMO 2026 collection (SFT and RL checkpoints, both training datasets, and Nemotron-IMO-Bench of 200 olympiad-level problems), the Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC model, and NeMo-Skills pipelines for IMO and IOI inference.
insights.speaker: Aleksander
insights.so_what: Open weights, data and recipes strengthen the Nemotron ecosystem versus closed frontier labs.
insights.locator: Open models, data, and recipes on Hugging Face
